context.challenge: Make org charts useful to managers, not another piece of enterprise overhead.
context.role: Product strategy, product design, brand design, and design-system lead
context.scope: Product direction, brand, user experience, and Sunny Peeps design system
context.body: The product began with the conviction that strong teams make healthy organizations. The chart is a means, not the purpose: it gives managers a way to see structure, update it as work changes, and bring a clear picture into conversations and decisions. That reframing set the direction for the strategy, the brand, and the design of the product itself.

sections.label: Product strategy
sections.title: The chart is a tool. The team is the point.
sections.description: The category often treats the diagram as the whole job. The strategy here starts with the manager: make a team's structure visible, then keep that picture useful as people and responsibilities change. The product should remove setup friction, invite active editing, and create a useful artifact without requiring a large enterprise suite or a consultant just to draw the chart.

sections.label: Brand · Sunny Peeps
sections.title: A challenger with an optimistic streak
sections.description: The brand was designed as an anti-hero: confident enough to challenge category incumbents and their enterprise overhead, while staying firmly on the manager's side. Sunny Peeps carries that point of view through a broad color spectrum representing the diversity of thought, color, creed, religion, culture, sexuality, and lived experience that healthy teams bring. In the interface, color distinguishes themes and departments; it never stands in for assumptions about an individual.
sections.imageAlt: Org Chart Studio's theme browser showing three visual directions for the same fictional team, alongside a larger preview.

sections.label: Product design · Import
sections.title: Start from the roster teams already have
sections.description: Spreadsheet import turns existing people data into a starting chart. Column mapping makes the interpretation visible before anything is confirmed. In this example, nine of ten rows are ready; one still needs a manager review.
sections.imageAlt: Import mapping dialog for fictional Northstar team data. Four columns are mapped; nine of ten rows are ready and one needs manager review.

sections.label: Import intelligence · Human review
sections.title: Automate the match. Keep the decision visible.
sections.description: A likely manager match is suggested, not silently applied. The manager can review the correction, accept it, and see the reporting line update. The product carries routine matching forward while leaving a consequential relationship under human control.

images.alt: Fictional Northstar import review showing a suggested match between the misspelled manager name Jordon Ellis and Jordan Ellis, waiting for confirmation.
The fictional Northstar import after confirmation: Theo Brooks reports to Jordan Ellis and the Needs manager count is zero.

sections.label: Product design · Guidance
sections.title: Help that stays beside the work
sections.description: A manager can read a short guide while keeping the chart in view, or choose Show me to be pointed to the real Reports to control. The guidance does not change the chart; it helps the person make the change themselves.

images.alt: A change-manager guide open beside the fictional Northstar org chart, with the chart still visible.
The Show me guide points to the Reports to control in the People table without changing the fictional chart.

sections.label: Product design · Export
sections.title: Design for where the chart goes next
sections.description: The product makes the handoff part of the experience: choose a format and scope, inspect page breaks, and preview the result before exporting. This fictional 14-person example plans seven team pages. PowerPoint exports use editable native shapes and text; PDF, PNG, and CSV support other ways teams share or reuse the information.
sections.imageAlt: Live export preview for a fictional 14-person organization, showing a team-level PowerPoint page and seven planned pages.

sections.label: Design leadership
sections.title: One point of view, carried through the product
sections.description: Strategy, brand, design system, and interaction design were treated as one connected problem. Sunny Peeps made the visual language reusable; the product carried it through chart editing, themes, import review, contextual help, and export. The result is not color for its own sake, but a more legible way for managers to see the people and structure behind the boxes.

projects.title: Unreel Recipes
projects.summary: Unreel Recipes is an experiment in building a fully agentic business. Instead of a traditional human team, the entire operation—product management, product design, social media marketing, and data analytics—is handed over to a swarm of independent AI agents. These agents coordinate, manage, iterate, and run the product autonomously.
projects.detail: The product turns a YouTube cooking video or recipe text into a permanent, source-credited recipe page, then offers a one-step-at-a-time Cook Mode for following along.

projects.title: Designer
projects.summary: An experimental agentic UX design harness that moves generative design upstream. Designer frames the problem, produces differentiated hypotheses, and builds selected directions into working prototypes so the ideas can be judged in use.
projects.detail: The useful result was not simply the interface. The experiment exposed where agentic design helped—and where it did not. Hypothesis generation produced genuinely different bets; a human-shaped canvas and adversarial evaluation loop became bottlenecks. Those findings now point toward a leaner, headless system of coordinating agents.

leadImage.alt: Designer canvas connecting a design brief and supporting inputs to three distinct product hypotheses and working prototype previews.

supportingImage.alt: Designer canvas with nodes for the brief, research, objectives, design system, constraints, and hypothesis incubator.
